4th Period.workingNow: Writing out your favorites list as paragraphs and pushing your changes.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A complete About Me page (copied from the Example file) with header/body structure, formatted favorites text, at least one resized image with a caption, and a table.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can write out a favorites list using paragraph tags so that my page has real content, ready to format tomorrow.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas.
agenda: I do: model a favorites list written in <p> tags (7 min)
We do: draft one favorites item together (5 min)
You do: self-paced — write out your full favorites list, commit + push (25 min)
Exit Ticket: how many favorites did you list? (3 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday we set up the structure. Today you got your favorites list written out and pushed. Tomorrow we go back in and format that same list with bold, italics, and headings.

6th Period.workingNow: Following along with a video to build the example state machine in Sprite Lab, independently.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A Sprite Lab or Game Lab project where a scene or sprite has at least two states triggered by an event.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can follow a tutorial to build a sprite with at least two states so that I see how an event triggers a state change.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including compound conditionals.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Entry routine — get set up independently at your own seat (3 min)
Watch: Sprite Lab state machine tutorial video, in full (10 min)
You do: follow the video step-by-step, building the exact example sprite (22 min)
Exit Ticket: what event triggers your sprite's change? (3 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday we sketched state diagrams on paper. Today you followed the tutorial video step-by-step and built the example sprite — a solid first rep with the tool. Tomorrow you'll take what you learned and apply it to your own design, working with a partner.
